analysis.answer: Current law sets the state minimum wage at $17.00 per hour. The measure lowers this rate to $15.00 per hour starting January 1, 2028.
Employers of minimum-wage workers benefit through lower mandatory labor costs. Minimum-wage workers pay the cost through a reduction in their legally guaranteed hourly earnings.

Employers may respond to the lowered wage floor by hiring more workers, increasing employee hours, or retaining a larger share of revenue. Workers earning the minimum wage may seek secondary employment, work more hours, or reduce household spending to compensate for lower hourly pay.

The effect of minimum wage changes on overall employment and hiring is widely disputed among researchers. Some find that lower minimum wages increase hiring by reducing the marginal cost of labor, while others find that minimum wage levels have little to no significant effect on overall job numbers, arguing that businesses adjust to wage requirements through minor price changes, improved productivity, or reduced turnover.

flags.note: The measure establishes a delayed effective date, waiting until 2028 to implement the new wage rate.
